dedupe_keys.name: whin open dataset of soil sensor and weather station data at production farms indiana

description: This dataset releases soil sensor data from three LoRa-connected IoT nodes, one on each of three production farms with soybean and corn fields near Purdue University in Indiana, each recording for five months, together with weather station data used to study how rain is absorbed into the soil. The nodes measure soil temperature, electrical conductivity and volumetric water content with Teros-12 sensors, plus air temperature and humidity, and send data over a custom LoRa protocol to Raspberry Pi gateways. It was produced by Charilaos Mousoulis, Pengcheng Wang, Saurabh Bagchi and colleagues at Purdue University as part of the five-year WHIN (Wabash Heartland Innovation Network) project and described in an arXiv paper of 16 February 2023. Coverage is a few fields in Indiana, United States. The dataset is offered free on a Purdue web page, which could not be reached from the cloud on the access date; the paper is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 and the dataset's own terms were not read. Caveats: only three nodes are released, the period is short, and rural IoT deployments suffer communication gaps that the authors discuss. For simulation it supplies real farm sensor streams for testing soil moisture models, irrigation digital twins and the reliability of rural sensor networks under drought or heavy rain. It is related to the SoilSense API record in this catalogue, a commercial source of similar sensor data.
